_doc: Fixture manifest for the multi-zoom sets (testset/zoomset_*), added 2026-08-19.
These are the FIRST real multi-zoom captures the project has ever had: one full-spread
anchor plus 2-4 phone zoom close-ups of the same spread, shot with the Android app
(app-android/) over Wi-Fi and processed by the desktop server. Until now Stage 01's
multi-zoom stitch path had only synthetic unit tests -- DEVICE_SESSION.md goal 3.
They were shot handheld with the book on the photographer's lap, so 40-55% of each
frame is room (floor, desk, cables, chair). That is not a flaw in the fixture; it is
what a real capture looks like, and it is what broke Stage 02 on three of the four.
MEASURED ON ARRIVAL (docs/RESULTS.md 2026-08-19):
- Stage 01 stitched 0 of 11 close-ups. Every one was rejected by the min_inliers=25
gate. Raising ORB's feature budget 4000 -> 20000 (no other change) takes it to 4 of 11.
- Cropping the anchor to the book by hand, with the budget already raised, added
almost nothing (de_01_f01 15->16 inliers, de_01_f02 43->46). So the clutter hurts
the GUTTER SPLIT, not the stitch; the stitch was starved of features.
- The seven that still fail are NOT explained by where their inliers sit: three of
them spread as widely across the frame as the four that pass. One (en_02_f02) got
WORSE with 5x the features. Page curvature under a planar homography is a suspect
with a mechanism and no evidence. OPEN.
- Stage 02 found the true spine on 1 of 4 spreads (zoomset_de_02).
NO GT of any kind yet. These are diagnostic fixtures, not graded ones.
Append-only, like every other testset entry.
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 (same day, later) -- the two MEASURED ON ARRIVAL bullets
about Stage 01 are WRONG and are kept above only so the correction is legible.
Re-measured with a correctness signal that does not come from the matcher
(photometric agreement after warping, eyeballed on full-res checkerboards):
- Stage 01 did not fail to LOCATE these close-ups. FIVE of the eleven were
located correctly by the shipped params, at 9-21 inliers, and thrown away
because min_inliers was 25 -- above every correct value in the corpus.
- The '4 of 11 at 20000 features' figure includes a FALSE POSITIVE:
en_01_f03 reaches 27 inliers on a warp that lands grass and sky where the
anchor has text. The budget change was not shipped.
- Blending the five correct registrations makes OCR WORSE (de_01 loses 178
high-confidence words). All five are SOFTER than the pixels they replace
(sharpness ratio 0.49-0.83), because a close-up must be warped down into
the anchor's frame and carries almost no extra resolution (scale 0.71-0.94).
- The six that never register are oblique views of a strongly CURVED page,
which confirms the curvature mechanism the arrival note listed as a
suspect with no evidence. The 'where the inliers sit' dead end still holds.
- Standalone OCR says the real finding is anchor CHOICE, not stitching: on
zoomset_de_02 the close-ups read 270 and 249 high-confidence words against
the anchor's 183, and Stage 01 picked the anchor.
Full writeup: docs/RESULTS.md 2026-08-19 'The gate was the bug, not the feature
budget'. Evidence: docs/data/stitch_and_orientation_20260819.json.
